title: Release State v1
description: The whole content of specs/releases/<release-id>/_RELEASE.json — ONE mutable JSON object, the release's current state, never an append-only event stream (operator ruling: 'e um arquivo altamente mutavel onde acompanhamos o estado do release. Nao faz sentido ser append-only' — retires release-event-v1.schema.json and its _RELEASE.jsonl fold, core/release_events.py). `phase`, `rc`, `defined`, `implemented`, `shipped` and `audited` are rewritten IN PLACE through core/atomic_write.py's compare-and-swap seam (expected_previous, refuse-stale) whenever a code path writes this document; an agent with file tools (product-engineer, at the phase boundaries this document's history used to record as separate `phase` lines) may also Read-then-Edit it directly, the same discipline a CAS write enforces mechanically. `defined`/`implemented`/`shipped`/`audited` are the four sha-bearing milestone facts (each set at most once meaningfully — a later legitimate rewrite is a correction, not a second append, so there is no more 'duplicate milestone' finding to detect: SPEC-DOC-043 retires with the JSONL fold it existed to police). `log` is the one place free-form governance narrative survives INSIDE this otherwise-typed document — the closure narrative (summary, size accounting, drifts, dispositions, artifact GC, intake candidates, rc ledger, archive decision) that _RELEASE.jsonl's `note` records used to carry, one entry per note, oldest first, never rewritten once appended.

schema.description: This schema's own id, carried in every document for a self-describing file.

release.description: Bare SemVer release id (e.g. '0.6.0') — matches the directory name this file lives under.

phase.description: The release's current lifecycle phase (DISCOVERY/DEFINITION/SPEC/PLAN/TASKS/IMPLEMENTATION/CLOSURE/ARCHIVED — the canonical vocabulary lives in core/release_state.py (PHASES), not duplicated here). Overwritten in place on every phase transition — no history of prior phases survives in this field; a transition worth remembering is recorded as a `log` entry.

rc.description: The current/most recent rc round number, or null before any rc round has opened.

defined.description: Set once, at the definition promotion commit (product-engineer). null before that point.

sha.description: The final-rc QA-close commit sha — not the merge commit (the two differ by the merge artifact).

rc.description: Which rc round closed this milestone.

implemented.description: Set once, at the final-rc QA close (qa-engineer). null before that point.

shipped.description: Set once, at the develop->main ship merge. null before that point.

sha.description: The sha the audit window reviewed this release at.

audited.description: Set (and may be overwritten) each time an audit window reviews this release's resolution. null before the first audit.

segment.description: OPTIONAL: the active dir-based segment (ADR-1/ADR-5) when the release's SPEC/PLAN/TASKS live under releases/<id>/<segment>/ rather than flat. Omitted or null for a flat (unsegmented) release.

log.description: Append-only governance narrative living inside this mutable document, oldest first. An entry is appended, never edited or removed once written.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp this note was appended.

agent.description: Agent or runtime that appended this note.

kind.description: Free-text category (e.g. 'note', 'closure-summary', 'closure-drift', 'closure-dispositions') — the closure-narrative `kind` vocabulary that used to live on _RELEASE.jsonl's `note` event's `data.kind`.
